<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via must_change_password (literal, a string literal in isForcedRotationPending))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (literal, 48 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a552e8699255db754446256aabac02c81ebd73a8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0daffe1d5cc46cfea449e1684fc7111be1f91259` — the merge of head `44d99fe72416bcac825e75e860e6453deb0a2eff` into base `a552e8699255db754446256aabac02c81ebd73a8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0daffe1d5cc46cfea449e1684fc7111be1f91259 && git checkout 0daffe1d5cc46cfea449e1684fc7111be1f91259
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a552e8699255db754446256aabac02c81ebd73a8 44d99fe72416bcac825e75e860e6453deb0a2eff && git checkout -B drift-repro a552e8699255db754446256aabac02c81ebd73a8 && git merge --no-ff 44d99fe72416bcac825e75e860e6453deb0a2eff

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a552e8699255db754446256aabac02c81ebd73a8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a552e8699255db754446256aabac02c81ebd73a8` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2a467e5fc0fbb35db9152cb49d3469cd2b39d8e5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-before-hook.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-password-session-policy.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/forced-password-change-new-password.test.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/RemediationOverlay.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/__tests__/RemediationOverlay.forcedResetNewPassword.test.tsx, ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/{ar,de,en,es,fr,ja,ko,pt,ru,zh}.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-after-hook.ts (the change / reset stamp and the sign-up stamp), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-password-session-policy.ts (`stampPasswordChangedAt`, `resolvePasswordChangeUserId`, `recordPasswordHistory`, the remediation gate that raises `PASSWORD_RESET_REQUIRED`), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-user-endpoints.ts and admin-import-users.ts (the flag's writers), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/internal-field-readback.ts (`recoverInternalFieldsForSystemRead`), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/package.json (`exports`), packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts (`must_change_password`), packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts (`PASSWORD_REUSE`, `PASSWORD_RESET_REQUIRED`), ui/packages/auth/src/createAuthClient.ts (the Console's change-password door), packages/objectql/CHANGELOG.md (the #22646 entry), scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs (the declaration prompt), review of record 6495005521 on #27477.

Face: narrowing. The diff touches no `packages/spec/src/**` non-test path and no governed path; the PR body declares `Clause-②: no` and the maintainer dispatched this review on the disclosure ruling. On this face the scope floor is every path of the diff outside the prose faces; the changeset is the lane seat's at ACCEPT and is read here only for ②.

Security-hardening ruling: this record names positions and refusals; it carries no reproduction.

### ① Derived judgments

The accept set and the served surface the diff changes, read off the code on this head:

1. **Forced-change refusal, both completion doors.** While `sys_user.must_change_password` is set, `/change-password` and `/reset-password` refuse a `newPassword` that verifies against the CURRENT credential hash with `400 PASSWORD_REUSE` and the forced-rotation message, whatever `passwordHistoryCount` is (the default 0 included). Coverage of the doors is complete: the only user-facing clearer of the flag is `stampPasswordChangedAt`, run by the after-hook on a successful `/change-password` or `/reset-password` (and on `/sign-up/email` for a user that did not exist, which is not a completion), and both doors pass the before-hook's `assertPasswordNotReused` first on the same `candidate`. The flag's writers are the administrator's doors (create-user, set-user-password, import-users) under system context. Correct.
2. **Order of refusals on `/change-password`.** The hook runs before better-auth's own verification of `currentPassword`, so the diff verifies the request's claim against the current hash first and judges the candidate only when the claim holds; an unconfirmed claim returns `undefined` and the endpoint answers its own `INVALID_PASSWORD`. Read off the code and the dev's ablation (`claimHolds = true` turned the wrong-claim case into `PASSWORD_REUSE`), consistent with better-auth's hook architecture. Correct, and it is wider than the body says: the gate sits ABOVE the history ring too, so with `passwordHistoryCount` greater than 0 a request with a wrong current password and a recycled new one, which answered `PASSWORD_REUSE` on `main`, now answers `INVALID_PASSWORD`. That closes a confirmation oracle over the history ring for a caller who holds a session but not the password, and it is a changed answer on an input that was already refused, not a narrowing. The changeset states it; the PR body does not (must-fix 2).
3. **`/reset-password`.** `currentPassword` is `undefined`, the claim holds by construction, and the token (resolved by `resolvePasswordChangeUserId` through `findVerificationValue`) is the authority. The forced refusal applies directly; a different password completes and the after-hook clears the flag. Correct.
4. **Return value and the ring.** With the flag set and depth 0 the function returns `undefined` after the forced check, so no history stash is made and the after-hook only stamps; with depth greater than 0 it falls through to the ring and returns `currentHash` exactly as on `main`. The after-hook's success test (`isAPIError`) is unchanged, so a refused change stamps nothing and the flag stays set, pinned at the door. Correct.
5. **Cost.** One `sys_user` read per `/change-password` and `/reset-password` always, even with depth 0 and no flag (pinned by the amended unit case: `findOne` sees `sys_user` and never `sys_account`); on `/change-password` the current password is now verified twice (the hook, then the endpoint), one extra scrypt per change. Acceptable for a credential door; noted.
6. **Fail-open.** `isForcedRotationPending` answers `false` on a lookup error, so a `sys_user` read failure lets the forced change complete with the same password, silently: no log line marks that the control did not run. The file's other reads fail open too, but the stamp beside them (`stampPasswordChangedAt`) logs a durability degradation when its write fails. Should-fix 1.
7. **`must_change_password` read.** The column is `readonly: true`, `group: 'Admin'`, not `internal`, so the system-context projection carries it; `=== 1` is read for SQLite drivers. Correct. The credential columns are recovered through `recoverInternalFieldsForSystemRead`, unchanged.
8. **Public surface.** `assertPasswordNotReused` is a private method on `AuthManager`; `FORCED_ROTATION_REUSE_MESSAGE` is exported from `auth-manager-password-session-policy.ts`, which `package.json` `exports` (`.`, `./client-address`, `./rate-limit-storage`) does not address and the entry does not re-export, so it is shipped bytes and not a published accept set. `PASSWORD_REUSE` and `PASSWORD_RESET_REQUIRED` are already ledger entries; the forced case is a second message under the existing code, whose condition is reuse of the current password, so the ledger does not move. `@object-ui/i18n` gains `auth.remediation.password.sameAsTemporary` in all ten packs (the key-parity test holds). Additive. Correct.
9. **Console.** `ChangePasswordForm` refuses locally only when `forcedReset` (gate `PASSWORD_RESET_REQUIRED`) and the typed new password equals the typed current one, before any request; `PASSWORD_EXPIRED` sends the same password on and the server judges it. The Console's `changePassword` is better-auth's `/change-password` under the bound client, so the server refusal in item 1 stays the authority for every client. Correct.
10. **Unchanged.** With no forced change outstanding, reuse is judged by `passwordHistoryCount` exactly as before, depth 0 accepting the same password (the control case). The administrator's set-user-password with the requirement switched off clears the flag by its own write and is not a user completion door. Correct.

### ② Semver level

Declared: `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`; `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@object-ui/app-shell`, `@object-ui/i18n` at `patch`.

**The arm is missing.** A request every holder of a forced-change flag could send on `main` and have accepted, `POST /api/v1/auth/change-password` or `/reset-password` with the new password equal to the current one on a deployment at the default history depth, is now refused `400`. That is an accept-set narrowing of a served runtime surface, the class `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` describes at its own prompt ("add `(narrowing)` if it narrows one, a BREAKING change, whatever its level") and the class the review of record 6495005521 on #27477 FAILed a bare `no` for today, with the dev adopting `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the next head (`5eb62f096`) and the PASS of record following; #22646 (`packages/objectql/CHANGELOG.md`, 18.0.0) is the template entry. The changeset's `feat` prefix and the body's own sentence ("the change now has to move the user to a new password") describe a tightening, and a client that automates a forced change with the issued password (an onboarding script, a test harness) breaks at this door. Measurable now: `node scripts/pm/check-owed-reviews.mjs` lists neither this PR nor #27431 among the PRs owing a contract review, because the face reader sees no arm and no path hit; the review the maintainer ordered is invisible to the sweep until the declaration says what the diff does.

What is right and stays: `Metadata-protocol: none` (no authorable key, value or type changes) and the `patch` level on all three packages (ruling A: a non-protocol narrowing ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING carriers). The changed answer in ① item 2 is a refusal-code change on an already-refused input; it belongs in the FROM / TO, not in the level. The arm owes the PR body a `Skills-docs:` line: no `skills/**` file teaches the forced password change, `passwordHistoryCount` or the change-password door, so `none — REASON` is the admissible value, read at ACCEPT.

### ③ Boundary flags

- (a) **"The flag read fails open (treated as not set) on a lookup error, as every read in `assertPasswordNotReused` already does."** Accepted as the file's posture; the silence is the finding (should-fix 1), not the direction.
- (b) **"The Console check compares the two typed strings; it never replaces the server's refusal."** Accepted; ① item 9.
- (c) **Body drift.** The PR body on this head is the pre-`2663005b6` account: "What changes" bullet 2 describes the claim check as the forced branch's alone, while the head gates the history ring too and changes the answer for a wrong-current, recycled-new request from `PASSWORD_REUSE` to `INVALID_PASSWORD`; the Tests section omits the three history-on cases the test file now carries; and "Verification" names its readings on `f1c03b281`, which two source-changing commits follow, so the body's evidence names a head that is not this head. The changeset (`2a467e5fc`) states the reorder correctly. Must-fix 2.
- (d) `open_questions`: the body lists none (「需要你做的:无」). Author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no login note owed.

### ④ Design judgment

On the narrowing face, against the published spec on `main`: the change takes no declared capability away at the consumer and makes the spec's own requirement real. `sys_user.must_change_password` is declared as "the user is blocked (403 `PASSWORD_RESET_REQUIRED`) until they change their password"; on `main` at the default history depth the change could be a no-op, so the flag cleared while the user kept the password the administrator knows, which defeats the only reason the flag exists. Judging reuse against the CURRENT hash under the flag, independent of `passwordHistoryCount`, is the narrowest rule that restores the declaration; keeping the code `PASSWORD_REUSE` keeps the ledger whole; reading both completion doors through the one hook that already owns reuse keeps a single rule. Placing every reuse refusal after the current-password claim is the right order for a credential door: a refusal that answers before the claim is confirmed is an oracle over the ring for a session holder without the password, and `/reset-password` is rightly exempt because its token is the claim. Judged per `hits` file:

- `auth-manager-password-session-policy.ts`: the forced read, the claim gate and the refusal are placed so that no path reaches a reuse answer before the claim holds, the depth-0 early return is preserved after the forced check, and the ring's return value is unchanged; holds.
- `auth-manager-before-hook.ts`: the claim is read only on `/change-password` and passed as `''` when absent, so an absent claim is refused by the endpoint's own schema rather than judged; holds.
- `auth-manager.ts`: the private method's docblock states the contract the module implements; holds.
- `forced-password-change-new-password.test.ts`: end to end through `handleRequest` over a real engine with the plugin's own manifest, so the `internal: true` strip and the readback are live; pins refusal, completion, the wrong-claim answer, both doors, the control and the three history-on orderings; holds. `auth-manager.test.ts`: the depth-0 case now pins the one `sys_user` read; holds.
- `RemediationOverlay.tsx` and its test: the local check is gated on the forced code only, and the test pins en and zh text, no request on a match, a different password sent, and the expiry screen unchanged; holds.
- The ten locale files: one key each; holds.

Ablation evidence in the body (forced refusal off, claim skipped, Console check off; each restored to the HEAD blob) is consistent with the pins read here and was taken on `f1c03b281`; the head's own evidence is CI's green `Test Core` and `Test UI` on `2a467e5fc`. Not re-run.

**Must-fix**

1. Declaration: in the changeset body and the PR body, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; keep `Metadata-protocol: none` and the three `patch` grades; add the `**BREAKING** (an accept-set narrowing)` banner with a FROM / TO paragraph (FROM: with the flag set and the default history depth, a change or reset to the same password completed and cleared the flag; a wrong current password with a recycled new one answered `PASSWORD_REUSE`. TO: refused `400 PASSWORD_REUSE` until a different password is chosen; a wrong current password answers `INVALID_PASSWORD` whatever the new one is); exactly one ADR-0087 HTML-comment marker in the changeset body, category `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, stating that no metadata key, spelling, export or stored shape moves and that what narrows is a credential door's accept set; and a `Skills-docs:` line in the PR body (② names the admissible value). Then re-run `pnpm check:adr-0087-registration` and `check-changeset-no-major` locally.
2. Body drift, in the same edit: "What changes" states that the claim gate sits above every reuse refusal, the forced one and the history ring's, and names the changed answer (`INVALID_PASSWORD` for a wrong current password whatever the new one is); the Tests section names the three history-on cases; "Verification" names the head it was read on, and states which readings are from `f1c03b281` and which (CI) are on `2a467e5fc`, or is re-read on the head.

**Should-fix**

1. When the `sys_user` flag lookup in `isForcedRotationPending` throws, log through the host's durability-degradation channel (as `stampPasswordChangedAt` does for its write) that the forced-change control did not run for this request, so a read outage of a security control is visible in the log rather than silent (① item 6).
2. `auth-manager.ts` docblock and the before-hook comment: say in one sentence that the gate is now above the history ring as well, so the next reader of `assertPasswordNotReused` does not take the forced branch for the only consumer of the claim.

Implemented-by: `claude/harden-forced-password-change`
Reviewed-by: `session_017xRBcVy4VXmkQjn2MGeaWk`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

The refusal covers both completion doors, the claim-first order closes an oracle, the ledger and the published surface do not move, and the Console keeps the server as the authority; the FAIL is the declaration and the body that no longer describes the head (must-fixes 1 and 2). A head that carries the corrected declaration and body and nothing else owes a delta review by this reviewer, not a full round.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
